title: Recorded Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections
description:
# Figure Description: `fig_intercept_error`

## Title and caption

- **Title:** Recorded Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections
- **Caption (for manuscript text only, excluded from figure visual):** One deterministic calculation evaluated on the same five observations used to determine the correction (b = 3). No stochastic repetitions, optimizer, external dataset, held-out evaluation, uncertainty intervals, or interpolated/extrapolated values are shown.

## Content: variable mapping

- **x-axis:** intercept correction *b*, continuous, label "Intercept correction b". Breaks at 0, 1.5, 3 with formatted labels "0", "1.5", "3".
- **y-axis:** mean squared error (MSE), continuous, label "Mean squared error (MSE)". Breaks at 0, 3, 6, 9.
- **Visual channels:** position only. Single series.
- **Geometry:** scatter points only. No connecting line, fitted curve, ribbon, or error bar.

## Complete list of plotted points

| # | b (x) | MSE (y) | Label above point | Source row in log |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 0 | 9 | "9" | Added b = 0 (MAE 3, MSE 9) |
| 2 | 1.5 | 2.25 | "2.25" | Added b = 1.5 (MAE 1.5, MSE 2.25) |
| 3 | 3 | 0 | "0" | Added b = 3 (MAE 0, MSE 0) |

## Presentation

**Canvas**
- Size: 5.0 in × 3.5 in, single-column manuscript figure.
- Background: white (`#FFFFFF`). No plot border.
- Font family: standard sans-serif (Helvetica / Arial / system sans).

**Axes**
- x-limits: [-0.25, 3.25]; breaks: c(0, 1.5, 3), labels: c("0", "1.5", "3").
- y-limits: [-0.5, 10]; breaks: c(0, 3, 6, 9).
- Axis lines: `#222222`, 0.4 pt linewidth on left and bottom edges.
- Tick marks: `#222222`, 0.4 pt, length 2.5 pt, outward.
- Tick labels: 10 pt, `#222222`.
- Axis titles: 12 pt, `#222222`.

**Title**
- 13 pt, bold, `#222222`, left-aligned at panel edge.
- Caption: Excluded from figure canvas per publication guidelines.

**Markers**
- Shape 16 (filled circle), size 3.2 mm diameter (approx. 9 pt).
- Fill and stroke: `#1F4E79`.

**Value labels**
- Text: "9", "2.25", "0", positioned 0.5 units above each point.
- Font: 10 pt, regular, `#1F4E79`.

**Grid**
- Major horizontal gridlines only: `#D9D9D9`, 0.3 pt linewidth.
- No vertical or minor gridlines.

**Legend**
- None (`legend.position = "none"`).

## Reproducibility code (R / ggplot2)

r
library(ggplot2)

df <- data.frame(
  b   = c(0, 1.5, 3),
  mse = c(9, 2.25, 0),
  lab = c("9", "2.25", "0")
)

p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = b, y = mse)) +
  geom_point(shape = 16, size = 3.2, colour = "#1F4E79") +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab), nudge_y = 0.5, size = 3.5,
            colour = "#1F4E79", family = "sans") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Intercept correction b",
                     breaks = c(0, 1.5, 3),
                     labels = c("0", "1.5", "3"),
                     limits = c(-0.25, 3.25)) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Mean squared error (MSE)",
                     breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 9),
                     limits = c(-0.5, 10)) +
  labs(title = "Recorded Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 10, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    plot.title         = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", colour = "#222222", hjust = 0),
    axis.title         = element_text(size = 12, colour = "#222222"),
    axis.text          = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#222222"),
    axis.line          = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, colour = "#222222"),
    axis.ticks         = element_line(linewidth = 0.4, colour = "#222222"),
    axis.ticks.length  = unit(2.5, "pt"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, colour = "#D9D9D9"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "none",
    plot.background    = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", colour = NA)
  )

ggsave("fig_intercept_error.pdf", p, device = cairo_pdf, width = 5, height = 3.5)
ggsave("fig_intercept_error.png", p, width = 5, height = 3.5, dpi = 300)
caption: Recorded mean squared error across three intercept corrections. Values correspond to one deterministic calculation evaluated on the same five observations used to determine the correction (b = 3), with no stochastic repetitions, optimizer, external dataset, held-out evaluation, uncertainty intervals, or interpolated values.

critic_history.suggestions:
1. **Caption Exclusion & Text Clipping**: The figure caption ('One deterministic calculation evaluated on the same five observations...') is currently rendered inside the image canvas via `labs(caption = ...)`. Per conference visual guidelines, captions must remain separate from the visual asset itself (to be placed in LaTeX/manuscript markup). Furthermore, in the rendered plot, this caption string is cut off and clipped at the bottom-right margin ('... (b = 3). No'). Remove `caption` from `labs()` and from `theme()`. 
2. **X-Axis Tick Label Formatting**: Because 1.5 is a floating-point value, ggplot formats the discrete numeric breaks as '0.0', '1.5', and '3.0'. Specify explicit tick labels `labels = c("0", "1.5", "3")` in `scale_x_continuous` to ensure consistent formatting that matches the data labels and raw records.
3. **Margins & Layout**: Removing the embedded caption cleans up the canvas bottom margin and prevents any risk of text truncation.

title: Residual-Based Intercept Correction on Five Observations
description:
**Figure description: `fig_residual_workflow` (diagram, LaTeX/TikZ)**

**Canvas and style**
- Pure white background, no outer frame border, no drop shadows, no gradients.
- Landscape canvas, dimensions approximately 17 cm × 6.8 cm, laid out strictly from left to right across 5 non-overlapping horizontal stages with generous spacing to avoid collisions and clipping.
- All text and math in Computer Modern: 8–9 pt for annotations, 9–10 pt for node labels, 10 pt for mathematical symbols.
- Rounded rectangular nodes with 3 pt corner radius, 0.6 pt outline, and light thematic fills:
  - Observations: pale blue fill `#DDEBF7`, outline `#2F5597`.
  - Baseline predictor: light gray fill `#EFEFEF`, outline `#595959`.
  - Residuals & scalar correction: pale orange fill `#FBE5D6`, outline `#C55A11`.
  - Corrected prediction: pale green fill `#E2F0D9`, outline `#548235`.
  - Evaluation: white fill, dark gray outline `#404040`.
- Arrows:
  - Solid computation/dependency arrows: 0.8 pt line width, dark gray `#333333`, `-Stealth` tips.
  - Dashed reuse path: 0.6 pt dashed (3 pt on, 2 pt off), color `#2F5597`, routed along the bottom row.

**Layout and elements (strictly non-overlapping, left to right)**

1. **Observation block (Column 1, centered vertically)**
   - A tall rounded box labeled 'Observations ($n = 5$)' at the top.
   - Contains a minimal two-column table:
     - Header: $x$ and $y = 2x+3$ separated by a horizontal rule.
     - Rows: $(-2, -1), (-1, 1), (0, 3), (1, 5), (2, 7)$.
   - Width ~3.0 cm, clearing Column 2 comfortably.

2. **Baseline predictor (Column 2, upper row)**
   - Positioned horizontally to the right of the Observation block (~0.8 cm horizontal clearance) and vertically aligned directly above the Residuals block.
   - Box labeled 'Fixed baseline' with $\hat{y}^{(0)} = 2x$.
   - Direct incoming solid arrow with right-angle step from the Observation block to the baseline box, labeled '$x$'.

3. **Residual computation (Column 2, lower row)**
   - Pale orange box positioned directly below the Baseline predictor box with clear vertical separation (~0.8 cm).
   - Labeled 'Residuals' with formula $r_i = y_i - 2x_i$.
   - Displays computed values: $r_i = 3, 3, 3, 3, 3$ ($i=1,\dots,5$).
   - Incoming solid horizontal arrow from the Observation block (labeled '$y_i$') and a vertical solid arrow from the Fixed baseline box above (labeled '$2x_i$').

4. **Scalar correction (Column 3, vertically centered with Residuals)**
   - Pale orange box placed strictly to the right of the Residuals box (~1.0 cm gap).
   - Contains formula $b = \frac{1}{5}\sum_{i=1}^{5} r_i = 3$.
   - Incoming horizontal arrow from Residuals to $b$.
   - Centered directly beneath this connecting arrow, the key annotation in 8 pt italic text without hyphenation: 'data dependency: correction computed\\from observed residuals' (using explicit multiline alignment to ensure no broken words like 'cor-rection').

5. **Corrected prediction (Column 4, vertically centered with Residuals and Column 3)**
   - Pale green box placed strictly to the right of Column 3 with ~1.0 cm horizontal clearance.
   - Labeled 'Corrected prediction' with formula $\hat{y}_i = 2x_i + b$.
   - Incoming arrow 1 (bypass): A compact orthogonal route starting from the top of the Fixed baseline box, traveling horizontally ~1.2 cm above Column 3, and descending into the top of the Corrected prediction box, labeled '$2x_i$' centered above the horizontal segment.
   - Incoming arrow 2: Horizontal solid arrow from the scalar correction box $b$ to the left edge of Corrected prediction, labeled '$+b$' centered clearly above the arrow.

6. **Evaluation block (Column 5, far right, vertically centered)**
   - White rounded box placed strictly to the right of Corrected prediction with clear separation (~1.0 cm gap).
   - Box width ~4.0–4.2 cm with `inner xsep=6pt` to prevent any text clipping:
     - Title: 'Evaluation on the same 5 observations'.
     - Math: $e_i = \hat{y}_i - y_i = 0$ (centered single line).
     - Note: 'finite arithmetic check, not generalization'.
   - Direct horizontal solid arrow from the right edge of Corrected prediction to the left edge of Evaluation, labeled '$\hat{y}_i$' clearly above the arrow segment.
   - Dashed blue reuse arrow originating from the bottom center of the Observation block, dropping into a dedicated lower corridor below all blocks, and entering the bottom of the Evaluation block. Labeled along the horizontal segment: 'same observations $(x_i, y_i)$ reused' in 8 pt blue text.

**Output format notes**
- Native editable `.tex` source ensuring coordinate/node positioning (`right=of ...`, `above=of ...`) with explicit bounding box and node widths preventing any text clipping or overlaps.
- Vector PDF and 300 dpi raster preview.
caption: Schematic of the residual-based intercept correction workflow on five synthetic observations. Baseline predictions 2x and observed targets y determine the residuals r_i, from which the mean correction b = 3 is computed. Adding this scalar offset produces corrected predictions 2x + b, which evaluate to zero residual error on the original data. The dashed path highlights the reuse of the five observations, underscoring that this procedure represents an exact finite arithmetic verification rather than predictive generalization.

critic_history.suggestions:
1. Severe Node Overlaps: Multiple nodes significantly collide and overlap due to insufficient horizontal and vertical node spacing:
   - The 'Fixed baseline' box directly overlaps the top-right of the 'Observations' box, obscuring the title and border.
   - The scalar correction box ($b = \frac{1}{5}\sum r_i = 3$) collides with and covers the right portion of the 'Residuals' box.
   - The 'Evaluation' box overlaps the right side of the 'Corrected prediction' box, truncating its label to 'Corrected predictio...'.
   Enlarge horizontal canvas spacing (or reduce node padding/width) so that each stage occupies a dedicated horizontal column with clear margins.
2. Text Formatting & Hyphenation: In the Evaluation block, awkward automatic line wrapping causes hyphenations ('arith-metic', 'gener-alization') and splits mathematical expressions ($e_i = \hat{y}_i -$ on one line and $y_i = 0$ on the next). Widen the evaluation block slightly to allow clean line breaks without mid-word or mid-formula hyphens.
3. Arrow Routing and Clarity:
   - The arrow from Observations ($x$) to Fixed baseline loops awkwardly over the top; position Fixed baseline cleanly to the right of Observations to allow a natural, direct arrow.
   - The connection from Corrected prediction to Evaluation loops awkwardly at the top border due to overlapping bounding boxes. A clean, horizontal arrow should connect the right edge of Corrected prediction directly to the left edge of Evaluation.

The node width must be expanded (to ~4.0–4.2 cm) with adequate inner margins (`inner xsep=6pt`) so that all lines render completely without clipping.
2. **Annotation Placement**: The italic note 'data dependency: correction computed from observed residuals' currently hangs directly under the 'Residuals' box. It should be centered cleanly underneath the horizontal arrow connecting 'Residuals' to the scalar correction box '$b$', which directly highlights the dependency relationship between those two stages.
3. **Horizontal Spacing**: The spacing between the scalar correction box ($b$) and the 'Corrected prediction' box is somewhat compressed, leaving very little room for the '$+b$' arrow and label. Increasing the gap between Column 3 and Column 4 by at least 0.4–0.6 cm will improve visual breathing room and readability.

- Landscape canvas, dimensions approximately 17 cm × 7.5 cm, laid out strictly from left to right across 5 non-overlapping horizontal stages with generous spacing to avoid collisions and clipping.
- All text and math in Computer Modern: 8–9 pt for annotations, 9–10 pt for node labels, 10 pt for mathematical symbols.
- Rounded rectangular nodes with 3 pt corner radius, 0.6 pt outline, and light thematic fills:
  - Observations: pale blue fill `#DDEBF7`, outline `#2F5597`.
  - Baseline predictor: light gray fill `#EFEFEF`, outline `#595959`.
  - Residuals & scalar correction: pale orange fill `#FBE5D6`, outline `#C55A11`.
  - Corrected prediction: pale green fill `#E2F0D9`, outline `#548235`.
  - Evaluation: white fill, dark gray outline `#404040`.
- Arrows:
  - Solid computation/dependency arrows: 0.8 pt line width, dark gray `#333333`, `-Stealth` tips.
  - Dashed reuse path: 0.6 pt dashed (3 pt on, 2 pt off), color `#2F5597`, routed along the bottom row.

**Layout and elements (strictly non-overlapping, left to right)**

1. **Observation block (Column 1, centered vertically)**
   - A tall rounded box labeled 'Observations ($n = 5$)' at the top.
   - Contains a minimal two-column table:
     - Header: $x$ and $y = 2x+3$ separated by a horizontal rule.
     - Rows: $(-2, -1), (-1, 1), (0, 3), (1, 5), (2, 7)$.
   - Keep width around 3.0 cm so it clears subsequent columns comfortably.

2. **Baseline predictor (Column 2, upper row)**
   - Positioned horizontally to the right of the Observation block (clearing its right border by at least 0.8 cm) and vertically aligned above the Residuals block.
   - Box labeled 'Fixed baseline' with $\hat{y}^{(0)} = 2x$.
   - Direct incoming solid arrow with right-angle step from the Observation block to the baseline box, labeled '$x$'.

3. **Residual computation (Column 2, lower row)**
   - Pale orange box positioned directly below the Baseline predictor box with clear vertical separation (~0.8 cm).
   - Labeled 'Residuals' with formula $r_i = y_i - 2x_i$.
   - Displays computed values: $r_i = 3, 3, 3, 3, 3$ ($i=1,\dots,5$).
   - Incoming solid horizontal arrow from the Observation block (labeled '$y_i$') and a vertical solid arrow from the Fixed baseline box above (labeled '$2x_i$').

4. **Scalar correction (Column 3, vertically centered with Residuals)**
   - Pale orange box placed strictly to the right of the Residuals box (clearing it with a 1.0 cm gap).
   - Contains formula $b = \frac{1}{5}\sum_{i=1}^{5} r_i = 3$.
   - Incoming horizontal arrow from Residuals to $b$.
   - Centered directly beneath this connecting arrow, the key annotation: 'data dependency: correction computed from observed residuals' in 8 pt italic text, with sufficient vertical clearance from both the box and the bottom reuse dashed line.

5. **Corrected prediction (Column 4, vertically centered)**
   - Pale green box placed strictly to the right of Column 3 with at least 1.0 cm horizontal clearance.
   - Labeled 'Corrected prediction' with formula $\hat{y}_i = 2x_i + b$.
   - Incoming arrow 1: A route from the top of the Fixed baseline box running horizontally above Column 3 and descending into the top of the Corrected prediction box, labeled '$2x_i$'.
   - Incoming arrow 2: Horizontal solid arrow from the scalar correction box $b$ to the left edge of Corrected prediction, labeled '$+b$' centered clearly above the arrow.

6. **Evaluation block (Column 5, far right, vertically centered)**
   - White rounded box placed strictly to the right of Corrected prediction with clear separation (at least 1.0 cm gap).
   - Generous box width (minimum 4.0–4.2 cm) with `inner xsep=6pt` to ensure zero text collision or border clipping:
     - Title: 'Evaluation on the same 5 observations' (fully visible without truncating 'observations').
     - Math: $e_i = \hat{y}_i - y_i = 0$ (centered on a single line).
     - Note: 'finite arithmetic check, not generalization' (fully visible without clipping 'check' against the right border).
   - Direct horizontal solid arrow from the right edge of Corrected prediction to the left edge of Evaluation.
   - Dashed blue reuse arrow originating from the bottom center of the Observation block, dropping into a dedicated lower corridor below all blocks, and entering the bottom of the Evaluation block. Labeled along the horizontal segment: 'same observations reused' in 8 pt blue text.

**Output format notes**
- Native editable `.tex` source ensuring coordinate/node positioning (`right=of ...`, `above=of ...`) with explicit bounding box and node widths preventing any text clipping or overlaps.
- Vector PDF and 300 dpi raster preview.

2. **Missing Label Consistency:** All major computation arrows feature explicit mathematical labels ($x$, $y_i$, $2x_i$, $+b$), but the arrow connecting 'Corrected prediction' to 'Evaluation' is unlabelled. Add the mathematical label '$\hat{y}_i$' directly above this connecting arrow to maintain consistent dataflow notation.
3. **Visual Balance & Routing:** The overhead bypass arrow routing $2x_i$ from 'Fixed baseline' to 'Corrected prediction' arches excessively high, creating a large, unbalanced void of negative space across the upper half of the figure. Reduce the vertical offset of this path so that it runs closer above the intermediate nodes without crowding, yielding a more compact, publication-ready aspect ratio.
4. **Observation Reuse Clarity:** Make the dashed reuse path label slightly more specific by denoting 'same observations $(x_i, y_i)$ reused', clarifying how both inputs and ground-truth targets enter the finite arithmetic evaluation.
